Power of the TOST or Noninferiority Test for a Linear Contrast

Source: R/power_equivalence_c.R
power_equivalence_c.Rd

Computes the exact power of the Schuirmann (1987) two one-sided tests procedure, or of the one-sided noninferiority test, for a linear contrast of group means \(\psi = \sum_j c_j \mu_j\) with one pooled error term, or for a contrast measured within each unit of a paired design. For equivalence, the power is the probability that the \((1 - 2\alpha)\) confidence interval for \(\psi\) lies entirely inside \((-\delta_L, \delta_U)\), computed by numerical integration over the chi distribution of the estimated error standard deviation; for noninferiority, the power is a noncentral t probability in closed form. This is the contrast generalization of power_equivalence_md.

Usage

power_equivalence_c(
  c_weights = NULL,
  n_per_group = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  true_sd,
  contrast_lower = NULL,
  contrast_upper = NULL,
  true_contrast = 0,
  alpha_level = 0.05,
  side = c("equivalence", "noninferiority"),
  df_error = NULL,
  design = c("independent", "paired")
)

Arguments

c_weights

The contrast weights, required for design = "independent". The weights must sum to zero with the positive weights summing to 1 and the negative weights to -1, so that the bounds are on the raw scale of the response. Leave NULL for design = "paired", where the weights are already in the per-unit contrast scores.

n_per_group

For design = "independent", the sample sizes per group (if length 1, equal group sizes are assumed); together with c_weights, n_per_group determines the standard error factor \(\sqrt{\sum_j c_j^2 / n_j}\). Leave NULL for design = "paired", which has no groups of different units and takes N; a paired call that gives n_per_group is refused.

N

For design = "paired", the number of units, each measured under every condition the contrast involves. Every unit contributes one contrast score, so this is the total sample size. Leave NULL for design = "independent", where the sizes are given per group in n_per_group; an independent call that gives N is refused.

true_sd

For design = "independent", the error standard deviation (the square root of the mean square error). For design = "paired", the standard deviation of the per-unit contrast scores (for two conditions, of the difference scores). It is \(\sigma\) in the formulas below.

contrast_lower, contrast_upper

Bounds on the raw scale of the response, each positive; the equivalence region is \((-\delta_L, +\delta_U)\), where \(\delta_L\) is contrast_lower and \(\delta_U\) is contrast_upper. For side = "equivalence", contrast_upper is required and contrast_lower defaults to it (symmetric bounds). For side = "noninferiority", the test is against \(-\delta_L\) alone, so contrast_lower is the argument to give; a call that gives only the upper bound uses it as the margin.

true_contrast

The population value of the contrast at which the power is evaluated (\(\psi\) in the formulas). Default 0, the most favorable point for an equivalence declaration.

alpha_level

One-sided significance level for each test. Default 0.05.

side

"equivalence" (default) for the TOST power, or "noninferiority" for the one-sided test against \(-\delta_L\).

df_error

The error degrees of freedom, \(\nu\) in the formulas below. Defaults to \(\sum_j n_j - J\) for design = "independent", the sum of n_per_group less the number of groups, and to \(N - 1\) for design = "paired"; supply it directly when the error term comes from a model with more groups or additional predictors than the contrast involves (for example, a five-group model supplying the pooled error for a two-group contrast).

design

"independent" (default) for groups of different units sharing one pooled error term, or "paired" for a contrast measured within each unit (two conditions, or a pre and a post measurement, on the same units), analyzed as the mean of the \(N\) per-unit contrast scores. The design decides which size argument is read: n_per_group for independent groups, N for a paired design. See Details.

Value

A one-row data.frame with columns term ("power") and value (the computed power, in \([0, 1]\)).

Details

Equivalence power. Conditional on the estimated error standard deviation \(S\), the \((1 - 2\alpha)\) CI fits inside the bounds on a computable event, and the unconditional power integrates that event over the scaled chi distribution of \(S\) on df_error degrees of freedom. With c_weights = c(1, -1) and equal n_per_group, the result reproduces power_equivalence_md exactly.

Noninferiority power. The one-sided test rejects when \(t = (\hat\psi + \delta_L)/\mathrm{SE}(\hat\psi)\) exceeds \(t_{1-\alpha,\nu}\), so the power is \(\Pr(T'_{\nu}(\lambda) > t_{1-\alpha,\nu})\) with noncentrality \(\lambda = (\psi + \delta_L)/(\sigma \sqrt{\sum_j c_j^2/n_j})\).

Paired designs. With design = "paired", each unit contributes one contrast score, \(d_i = \sum_j c_j y_{ij}\), and the analysis is of their mean: the standard error is \(\sigma / \sqrt{N}\) on \(N - 1\) degrees of freedom, where \(N\) is the number of units (the argument N), so \(\sqrt{\sum_j c_j^2 / n_j}\) above becomes \(1 / \sqrt{N}\) and both powers are computed as for the independent design. The weights that form the scores should follow the same rule as c_weights (positive weights summing to 1, negative to -1), so that the bounds are on the raw scale; for two conditions the score is the difference. Its standard deviation true_sd carries the correlation between the measures: for two measures with a common standard deviation \(\sigma_y\) correlated \(\rho\), it is \(\sigma_y \sqrt{2(1 - \rho)}\), smaller than \(\sigma_y \sqrt{2}\), the standard deviation of a difference between independent observations, whenever \(\rho > 0\); that is the precision a paired design buys.

The feasibility condition. If the expected half-width of the CI is not smaller than the bounds allow, the equivalence power is zero or near zero regardless of true_contrast: an imprecise design cannot declare equivalence even when the arms are truly identical. Planning should target a half-width of about half the bound; see ss_power_equivalence_c and ss_aipe_c.

References

Chattopadhyay, B., Bandyopadhyay, T., Kelley, K., & Padalunkal, J. J. (2025). A sequential approach for noninferiority or equivalence of a linear contrast under cost constraints. Psychological Methods, 30(2), 425–439. doi:10.1037/met0000570

Phillips, K. F. (1990). Power of the two one-sided tests procedure in bioequivalence. Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Biopharmaceutics, 18(2), 137–144. doi:10.1007/BF01063556

Schuirmann, D. J. (1987). A comparison of the two one-sided tests procedure and the power approach for assessing the equivalence of average bioavailability. Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Biopharmaceutics, 15(6), 657–680.

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# 1. Two groups of 61 and 113 sharing a five-group pooled error term
#    (so df_error = 404 - 5 = 399), bounds of 5 raw-scale points:
#    the design's probability of declaring equivalence when the
#    groups are truly identical.
power_equivalence_c(c_weights = c(1, -1), n_per_group = c(61, 113),
                    true_sd = 15.67, contrast_upper = 5,
                    true_contrast = 0, df_error = 399)
#>  term  value
#>  power 0.281

# 2. The same design's noninferiority power at the same point.
power_equivalence_c(c_weights = c(1, -1), n_per_group = c(61, 113),
                    true_sd = 15.67, contrast_upper = 5,
                    true_contrast = 0, df_error = 399,
                    side = "noninferiority")
#>  term  value
#>  power 0.641

# 3. Agreement with power_equivalence_md() in the two-group case
#    (Phillips, 1990, Table 1: expected 0.8029678).
power_equivalence_c(c_weights = c(1, -1), n_per_group = 24, true_sd = 0.20,
                    contrast_lower = 0.2, contrast_upper = 0.2,
                    true_contrast = 0.05, df_error = 22)
#>  term  value
#>  power 0.803

# 4. A paired design: 50 units measured under both conditions, with
#    difference scores whose SD is 1, and a noninferiority margin of
#    0.5. No upper bound is needed for a noninferiority question.
power_equivalence_c(N = 50, true_sd = 1, contrast_lower = 0.5,
                    side = "noninferiority", design = "paired")
#>  term  value
#>  power 0.967
